paper.title: Online Learning for Multi-Layer Hierarchical Inference under Partial and Policy-Dependent Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-layer hierarchical inference routing with terminal-only, policy-dependent feedback (node-level contextual bandit with threshold-destination experts)
unmapped: Loss of a node is observed only if the job reaches the terminal oracle layer; observation probability is policy-dependent and decays with depth (not standard bandit feedback)
Loss defined recursively across layers of a hierarchy of decentralized learners
Long-term per-node resource constraints handled via Lyapunov virtual queues
Job arrivals i.i.d. with bounded first and second moments (Assumption 3.1); no stochastic assumption on induced losses
Context = (task type, confidence score); experts are threshold-destination pairs
Periodic model placement under memory constraints
settings.definition_quote: We model HI routing as a decentralized online learning problem with partial and policy-dependent feedback. ... Feedback is revealed only if a job is routed to the oracle layer; as a result, the probability of observing loss at a node depends recursively on downstream routing decisions under the global policy.

symbols.N_exp: |E_n(y)|, number of joint threshold-destination experts at node n for task type y
symbols.V_sum: sum over jobs of E[1{y(j)=y} 1{n on path} V_{n,y}(j)], V_{n,y}(j) = weighted mean plus max of squared variance-reduced loss estimates

conditions: eta * F_max < 1 where F_max bounds the shifted estimator (used in proof)

source.label: theorem:regret
source.quote: For $\eta > 0$, the expected node-level regret $R_{n,y}(\Gamma)$ relative to the best fixed threshold-destination pair $(h^*, n'^{*}) \in \mathcal{E}_n(y)$ is strictly bounded by R_{n,y}(\Gamma) \le \frac{\ln(|\mathcal{E}_n(y)|)}{\eta} + \eta \sum_{j=1}^\Gamma \mathbb{E}[ ... V_{n,y}(j) ]

results.notes: Horizon measured in jobs Gamma. Regret is node-level, per task type, defined with min outside expectations (pseudo-regret style). Bound is data-dependent via variance proxy; paper remarks eta ∝ 1/sqrt(Gamma) gives O(sqrt(Gamma)). Feedback mapping to 'bandit' is approximate.

symbols.Psi_max: uniform bound on expected variance term

conditions: best discretized policy satisfies resource constraints

source.label: cor:optimality
source.quote: By setting the learning rate to $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal{Y}| \ln |\mathcal{E}_{max}|}{\Gamma \Psi_{max}}}$, the optimality gap of the proposed VR-Ly-EXP4 algorithm is strictly bounded by: $$\Phi_\Gamma(\boldsymbol{\pi}) - \Phi_\Gamma(\boldsymbol{\pi}^*) \le \frac{\alpha}{v \bar{A}} + \frac{2 |\mathcal{N}|}{v} \sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal{Y}| \Psi_{max} \ln|\mathcal{E}_{max}|}{\Gamma}} + \varepsilon_0$$

results.notes: Bound on time-averaged expected inference error gap versus optimal continuous routing policy (per-job average, not total regret). Requires Gamma and Psi_max to tune eta.
